daily.ideas: Company Update: GAMUDA; Economic Viewpoint: Malaysia 2027 Federal Budget Preview

news.h: Powerwell secures RM190.4m orders to supply low voltage switchgear for data centre in Johor
news.body: Powerwell Holdings Bhd said it has secured two contracts worth RM190.4m for the supply of low-voltage switchgear and related equipment for a data centre project in Johor. The electrical equipment manufacturer said its wholly owned unit, Powerwell International Sdn Bhd, will be supplying the equipment to a multinational technology corporation specialising in data centres. The group did not disclose the name of the corporation in its statement, saying only that it is a returning customer. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: It is the largest award in the company's history and the comparison is available. Powerwell's previous largest was RM158.8m, also for a Johor data centre, headlined in June 2026 by The Edge Malaysia, the New Straits Times and The Sun as the largest in company history. RM190.4m is 19.9% above that, computed here. The item gives no delivery schedule, no margin and no split between the two orders, so nothing can be annualised - which is the difference between this and the construction awards this board carried yesterday, all of which stated a duration.

The customer is described but not named, and the description is the informative part. A multinational technology corporation specialising in data centres, and a returning customer - so this is most likely repeat business from the counterparty behind the June order, which the item does not say and this board cannot establish from the retrieved source. No country, no operator name, no site and no capacity for the data centre appears.

Low-voltage switchgear places Powerwell one layer further inside the building than yesterday's headline award. On 21 September this board carried Jati Tinggi's RM72.8m contract for a 275kV high-voltage cable connection to a data centre landing station - grid connection. Switchgear is the electrical distribution equipment on the other side of that connection. Two consecutive editions have now carried two different tiers of the same buildout, and neither item mentions the other; the pairing is made here.

Johor remains the centre of gravity for this board's data centre flow and this is the second-largest single award in the run. Recent entries: CBH Engineering's RM60.0m (27 August) and RM88.1m Selangor job (8 September), TRC Synergy's RM150m hyperscale subcontract from a Gamuda unit (9 September), Paragon Globe's RM45.2m Johor development contract (11 September), KGB's RM1.83b semiconductor wafer-fab award (15 September) and Jati Tinggi's RM72.8m (21 September). Only KGB's is larger.

This board holds no Kenanga coverage of Powerwell, and the 22 September bundle - one Company Update and one Economic Viewpoint - contains no electrical-equipment report. The nearest Kenanga demand figures here are from its 21 September TENAGA Company Update, which puts data centre investment at more than 8,000MW by 2035 with about 700MW coming on stream this year, and its Renewable Energy Sector Update, which puts Malaysia's secured data centre maximum demand at about 8.35GW today against a PETRA projection of about 21GW by 2040.

news.h: Winstar Capital plans RM300.0m sukuk for investments, land acquisition, refinancing
news.body: Winstar Capital Bhd proposes to issue a RM300.0m sukuk to finance investments and land acquisition, as well as to refinance existing loans. The group, which lodged the sukuk murabahah programme with the Securities Commission Malaysia on Monday (Sept 21), said proceeds will also be used to defray issuance expenses and for working capital. Winstar Capital said the programme carries a tenure of 30 years, with the first issuance expected within 90 business days of lodgement. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: The 30-year tenure is the striking term and the item prints no price for it. No profit rate, no tranche structure, no credit rating, no principal adviser and no security package is given, so a RM300.0m facility running to 2056 cannot be assessed on cost at all. The only timing figure is the first issuance, expected within 90 business days of the 21 September lodgement - roughly late January 2027 on a five-day week, computed here.

A lodged programme is a ceiling, not a drawdown, and the item does not make that distinction. RM300.0m is the maximum issuable across the life of the sukuk murabahah programme; the cash actually raised in the first issuance could be a fraction of it. Nothing here tells a reader how much debt Winstar is adding in the next year.

Four uses of proceeds are listed and none is sized: investments, land acquisition, refinancing of existing loans, issuance expenses and working capital. Without a split, the item cannot be read as growth funding or as balance-sheet repair, and no existing borrowings figure is given to measure the refinancing portion against.

It is the only debt-capital-markets item in the edition, and three of the five corporate items today are balance-sheet exercises rather than trading news - this, Excel Force's RM11.0m placement and Straits Energy's RM90.0m capital reduction. The nearest prior comparable on this board is Central Global's up-to-RM83.0m private placement for Sabah construction projects, carried on 3 September.

This board holds no Kenanga coverage of Winstar Capital and the 22 September bundle carries no report on corporate sukuk or credit markets. Kenanga's fixed-income work on this board runs through its Bond Market Weekly Outlook, most recently on 21 September, which covers sovereign MGS, GII and foreign bond flows rather than corporate issuance.

news.h: Excel Force proposes RM11.0m placement for working capital after TS Wong sell-off
news.body: Excel Force MSC Bhd, one of the companies linked to businessman Wong Thean Soon, has proposed a private placement to raise up to RM11.0m for working capital and free up funds for a software project. The move comes about three weeks after Wong was forced to sell more than two-thirds of his stake in the financial technology solutions provider. Excel Force plans to issue up to 61.0m new shares, representing 10.0% of its existing issued share capital, to third-party investors to be identified later. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: The implied issue price is the one number the item permits: up to RM11.0m across up to 61.0m new shares is about RM0.180 a share, computed here. The item prints no market price, so whether that represents a discount cannot be established from the retrieved source, and Excel Force does not appear in this edition's top-volume, top-gainer or top-loser tables.

The placement size also gives the share base. If 61.0m new shares are 10.0% of existing issued share capital, the existing base is about 610m shares, computed here, rising to about 671m on full take-up - so incoming investors would hold about 9.1% of the enlarged capital. The placees are 'to be identified later', so no name, no lock-up and no resulting shareholding structure is disclosed.

The timing is the substance. The raise comes about three weeks after Wong Thean Soon was forced to sell more than two-thirds of his stake, so the company is issuing equity into a disposal overhang rather than from a position of strength. The item does not say who acquired the forced-sale shares, what price they went at, or whether Wong retains any board role.

Use of proceeds is stated loosely and the operative part is undescribed. Working capital, plus freeing up funds for a software project that is not named, sized, dated or attributed to a customer. At up to RM11.0m this is the smallest capital-raising this board has carried, an order of magnitude below Winstar's RM300.0m sukuk in this same edition.

This board holds no Kenanga coverage of Excel Force and no coverage of any Malaysian fintech or software name. The technology names Kenanga has covered here are semiconductor and hardware - INARI (1 September), KGB (15 September), NATGATE, OPPSTAR, MPI and D&O - and the 22 September bundle contains no technology report.

news.h: Inspace Creation bags RM34.8m subcontract for renovation works
news.body: Interior fit-out firm Inspace Creation Bhd has won a subcontract of RM34.8m to undertake renovation works on commercial properties. The group stated that its indirectly wholly owned subsidiary, IDPM Builder Sdn Bhd, had accepted a letter of award for the project from an undisclosed customer on Monday (Sept 21). The company said it could not disclose the identity of the main contractor as well as the location of the project and specific details of the subcontract due to confidentiality and non-disclosure obligations. The contract, which takes effect upon acceptance, is scheduled to conclude in July 2028. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: Duration supplies the only run-rate. Effective on acceptance on Monday 21 September and concluding in July 2028 is about 22 months, so RM34.8m works out at roughly RM1.6m a month, computed here. No margin, no retention terms and no payment milestones are stated, so the earnings contribution cannot be sized.

Disclosure is thinner here than on any contract award this board has carried. The customer is undisclosed, the main contractor cannot be named, the location is withheld and the specific scope is withheld - all attributed to confidentiality and non-disclosure obligations. What remains verifiable is a value, a subsidiary, an acceptance date and an end date.

The subsidiary is described as indirectly wholly owned, so the full value accrues to the group but through at least one intermediate company. That is a marginally longer chain than the directly wholly owned structures in the 21 September edition - Vestland Infra, TSR Bina and Jati Tinggi Holding - and the item names no intermediate entity.

Interior fit-out is a new category for this board and it sits at a different point in the cycle from everything around it. The construction awards carried over the past fortnight have been civil, earthworks, M&E and cable works - Citaglobal (14 September), GFM and Exsim Hospitality (15 September), Crest Builder and PTT Synergy (17 September), Enproserve (18 September), Vestland, TSR Capital and Jati Tinggi (21 September). Renovation of completed commercial property is later-cycle work than any of them; that reading is drawn here, since the item supplies no context.

This board holds no Kenanga coverage of Inspace Creation, and the 22 September bundle carries no construction or building-materials report. The only Kenanga construction figures in today's bundle are in the GAMUDA Company Update, whose peer table covers just IJM, KERJAYA, KIMLUN and SUNCON.

news.h: Straits Energy Resources proposes capital reduction to wipe out RM90.0m in losses
news.body: Straits Energy Resources Bhd has proposed a share capital reduction to eliminate RM90 million in accumulated losses. Based on the latest unaudited results, the proposed share capital reduction would eliminate the group's RM39.2m accumulated losses as of June 30, 2026 - resulting in retained earnings of RM50.8m, before taking into account the estimated RM165,000 expenses related to the exercise as well as the foreign currency translation reserve of RM4.1m. On the company level, the share capital reduction will eliminate part of its accumulated losses of RM101.9m, leaving accumulated losses of RM11.9m. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: The arithmetic reconciles in both directions and the item prints the parts without showing the check. At group level, applying RM90.0m against RM39.2m of accumulated losses at 30 June 2026 leaves RM50.8m of retained earnings, and RM39.2m plus RM50.8m is exactly RM90.0m. At company level, RM101.9m less RM90.0m leaves RM11.9m, also exact. Both computed here.

It moves nothing in cash. A share capital reduction transfers value from share capital to retained earnings; no money enters the company, no borrowing is repaid and no asset changes hands. What it creates is distributable reserves, since dividends are paid out of retained earnings - and the item does not mention dividends at all.

Two deductions are flagged but not applied to the headline. About RM165,000 of expenses for the exercise and a foreign currency translation reserve of RM4.1m sit outside the RM50.8m figure, which is stated as being before both. The post-exercise position is therefore lower than the headline number by an amount the reader is left to net off.

The gap between group and company is the part that limits what this achieves. The company carries RM101.9m of accumulated losses against the group's RM39.2m, so the deficit is concentrated at the level a distribution would have to be paid from, and even after the reduction the company remains RM11.9m in deficit. On that basis the exercise does not by itself restore dividend capacity at the company level; that conclusion is drawn here and the item states no intention either way.

This board holds no Kenanga coverage of Straits Energy Resources, and the item gives no description of the company's business. Kenanga's oil and gas coverage here runs through KEYFIELD (18 September), UZMA (1 September), DAYANG, VELESTO, ARMADA, WASCO and MISC, and the 22 September bundle carries no oil and gas report.

macro.h: Greer says US, China to continue talks on trade truce extension
macro.body: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer indicated that the country and China remain divided on the terms of a trade truce extension, suggesting that three to six months is a range that Washington could support. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: It supplies the first quantified parameter in a sequence this board has been carrying blind. On 21 September the lead global item was 'Trump-Xi showdown casts shadow over global economy', with no date, no venue, no agenda and no negotiating position. Today the US Trade Representative attaches a range to one variable: three to six months is what Washington could support for a truce extension.

The framing is still division, not progress. The two sides 'remain divided on the terms'. No expiry date for the current truce, no tariff rates, no product scope and no meeting date is given, so the three-to-six-month range cannot be anchored to a calendar and a later edition has nothing precise to measure against.

Kenanga's own research puts this at the centre of the week's rates view. Its 21 September Bond Market Weekly Outlook names the Trump-Xi meeting twice as a key driver for both Malaysian government securities and US Treasuries, and states that 'any trade or de-escalation breakthrough would likely reduce UST duration demand' - that is, a breakthrough pushes Treasury yields up. A three-to-six-month extension defers the question rather than resolving it, which on Kenanga's own framing is the outcome that keeps yields rangebound.

Malaysia's exposure to this is concentrated and this board holds the figure. Kenanga's 21 September External Trade Economic Viewpoint puts August electrical and electronic exports at +66.5% year-on-year and 48.4% of total exports, with shipments to the United States at a record +139.1%. A rolling three-to-six-month truce leaves roughly half the export book on a short renewal horizon.

The Prime Minister leaves for China the same day, and no source connects the two. This edition separately carries Anwar travelling to Shanghai and Hangzhou from Tuesday for digital trade and TVET. Malaysia is deepening bilateral ties with one party to a dispute whose terms are being set in Washington; the grouping is made here. No report in the 22 September bundle carries a Kenanga view on US-China trade policy.

macro.h: US investments in Spain surge 84% despite political tensions
macro.body: US investments in Spain jumped 84% in the first half of 2026, as investors brushed aside political tensions between the two countries. American investment in Spain grew by 84% in the six-month period from a year earlier, according to government data published Monday. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: One growth rate, one period, and no base. The item gives no euro or dollar amount, no prior-year level, no sector split and no comparison with other destinations, so the absolute size of the flow cannot be established from the retrieved source.

Percentage growth without a base is the weakest statistic this board carries. An 84% rise on a depressed first half of 2025 and an 84% rise on a strong one are different facts, and the item distinguishes neither. It also does not say whether the measure is announced investment, committed capital or completed transactions.

The stated angle is political and it is equally unsized. Investors 'brushed aside political tensions between the two countries' - but no policy, no dispute, no date and no affected sector is identified, so the contrast the item is built on cannot be tested.

It is the second European item in the edition and the two have nothing in common. The other is the ECB launching blockchain settlement for tokenised wholesale transactions. Recent European entries on this board have been monetary or shock-driven - the ECB hike on 11 September, Lagarde on 14 September, Kazaks on 15 September, the proposed EU windfall tax on energy companies on 21 September - and today's pair is neither.

There is no Malaysian read-across and no Kenanga view. No listed Malaysian company is named, no sector is identified, and the 22 September bundle - a GAMUDA Company Update and a domestic budget preview - carries nothing on Spain, the euro area or cross-border foreign direct investment.

macro.h: Merdeka giveaways set election pace; revenue base stays narrow
macro.body: Budget 2027 is the fifth MADANI Budget and the second year of 13MP, built around 10 focus areas. It aims mainly at the cost of living, easing financial pressure on households, especially the M40 group, amid global energy challenges. (See Economic Viewpoint: Malaysia 2027 Federal Budget Preview)
takeaways: This is Kenanga's own publication surfacing in the digest rather than third-party news, and it is the reason today's line-up is two reports and not one. The Ideas of the Day line names only GAMUDA; this Economic Viewpoint appears only here, in Macro Bits, with a 'See Economic Viewpoint' pointer. The full note is carried as its own row on this board and every figure there is read from the PDF - see Malaysia 2027 Federal Budget Preview, and the flag on that row about how it is dated and filed.

The digest line carries the framing and omits the call. Budget 2027 is the fifth MADANI Budget and the second year of the 13th Malaysia Plan, built around ten focus areas, aimed mainly at cost of living and the M40 group, with growth priorities in AI, semiconductors and the digital economy. What it does not say is that Kenanga reads the budget as having no revenue-reform pillar at all.

The sharper claims sit in the note. Kenanga forecasts the federal deficit at 3.8% of GDP in 2026 (2025: 3.7%) narrowing to 3.5% in 2027, projects net expenditure down to RM448.0b from RM453.0b, and reads Budget 2027 as a pre-election budget 'possibly on a shorter runway than February 2028 implies', with 2Q27 as its working assumption for GE16.
One hard date the digest line omits and the note states: Budget 2027 will be tabled on 9 October 2026 - seventeen days after this edition.

This board has tracked Budget 2027 since before the fiscal detail existed: cost-of-living focus and investment attraction (24 August), Home Ownership Campaign and EV infrastructure proposals (26 August), and the BUDI95 quota restoration to 300 litres a month taking effect (1 September). Today's note is the first full Kenanga preview of the budget carried on this board.

macro.h: Anwar to visit China from Tuesday for diplomacy, digital trade and TVET
macro.body: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's visit to Shanghai and Hangzhou starting from Tuesday is aimed at deepening economic ties, advancing digital trade frameworks and highlighting the importance of technical talent development. (The Malaysian Reserve)
takeaways: Three stated purposes and no deliverables. Deepening economic ties, advancing digital trade frameworks and highlighting technical and vocational education and training, across Shanghai and Hangzhou from Tuesday - that is, today. No duration, no delegation, no counterpart named, no agreements to be signed and no institutions or companies to be visited appear.

The trade base is large and this board holds a named figure for it. Malaysia-China bilateral trade rose 30.6% to USD80.4b in the first half of 2026, carried on this board on 4 September from the deputy minister. Nothing in today's item updates that or attaches a target to the visit.

It lands the same day as the edition's lead global item on the US-China truce talks, and neither item mentions the other. Malaysia is travelling toward Beijing while Washington negotiates the terms of a truce with it; the pairing is made here, and the digest presents them as unrelated bullets in different regions.

It is the latest in a run of foreign-policy items this board has carried without a single figure attached to an outcome: the BRICS summit visit to India and meetings with Modi and Putin (11 September), semiconductor cooperation with Modi and a special mechanism with Putin (14 September), and the fairer-global-order framing (15 September). The pattern is consistent bilateral economic diplomacy with non-Western partners; the results remain unquantified on this board.

No report in the 22 September bundle carries a Kenanga view on China or on Malaysia's external relations - its Economic Viewpoint today is domestic and fiscal. The nearest relevant Kenanga figure on this board is the 21 September External Trade note putting August exports at RM191.05b, up 45.5%, with a record concentration in shipments to the United States.

macro.h: Mihas 2026 expected to attract 50,000 visitors from 45 countries - Matrade
macro.body: The 22nd Malaysia International Halal Showcase (Mihas), opening at the Malaysia International Trade and Exhibition Centre (Mitec) this Wednesday, is expected to attract 50,000 visitors from 45 countries. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: Two figures, a venue and a date: 50,000 visitors from 45 countries at MITEC from Wednesday, for the 22nd edition of the showcase. Expected, not achieved - and there is no prior-year comparison, no exhibitor count, no floor space and no trade-value target, so the event cannot be sized against last year from the retrieved source.

The figure is the organiser's forecast about its own event. Matrade both runs the showcase and supplies the projection, which makes this a target rather than data, and it should be read that way until an outturn is published.
There is no economic content beyond attendance. No sales value, no MoU pipeline, no participating listed companies and no product-category breakdown appears, so nothing here reaches a security.

It belongs with the edition's other unquantified tourism and events items rather than with trade policy. This edition also carries Malaysia expanding air links with the UAE and GCC, and Kenanga's own Budget Preview in this bundle names the 34th SEA Games across Kuala Lumpur, Sarawak, Penang and Johor as a 2027 tourism support. The first two are about 2026 arrivals and Kenanga's is about 2027; the grouping is made here.

This board holds one prior tourism datum - over 21 million international tourists visited Malaysia in the first half of 2026, carried on 26 August - and no Kenanga coverage of a halal-sector name. No report in the 22 September bundle covers consumer, retail or travel.

macro.h: Malaysia expands air links with UAE, GCC to boost tourist arrivals
macro.body: Malaysia is strengthening air connectivity and tourism cooperation with the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and the wider Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) region to boost tourist arrivals from the Middle East. (The Malaysian Reserve)
takeaways: There is no number in it at all. No route, no airline, no frequency, no seat capacity, no bilateral agreement, no target arrivals and no timeline is given - only that connectivity and tourism cooperation are being strengthened with the UAE and the wider GCC.

Unquantified is not the same as unimportant, but it does mean nothing can be tracked. A later edition will have nothing to compare this against, the same limitation this board recorded on 21 September for Bank Negara's SME liquidity assessment.

The demand side is entirely absent. No current arrivals figure from the Middle East, no share of total tourist arrivals and no spend-per-visitor appears, so the incremental opportunity cannot be sized even in order-of-magnitude terms.

The listed exposure is obvious in kind and absent in name. Airlines, airport operators and hotel owners are the channel, and the item names none of them. This board holds no Kenanga coverage of a Malaysian airline, airport operator or hotel group, so there is no row here that this would read across to.

With Mihas and the SEA Games reference in Kenanga's own Budget Preview, tourism is the edition's quiet recurring theme - three separate mentions, none of which reaches a figure that a listed company could be measured against. No report in the 22 September bundle covers the sector.

macro.h: Thailand considering oil tax cut, finance minister says
macro.body: Thailand is considering an oil tax cut, Finance Minister Ekniti Nitithanprapas said on Monday. Ekniti said cutting the excise tax on fuel would help ease the cost-of-living burden on the public caused by the energy crisis. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: It is a consideration, not a decision, and nothing about it is sized. Thailand 'is considering' an excise tax cut on fuel, stated by the finance minister on Monday - with no rate, no revenue cost, no effective date and no product scope. There is no way to judge the fiscal impact from the retrieved source.

The stated motive is the region's dominant policy problem and the chosen instrument is a third distinct one. Malaysia's response to the same energy shock was to widen a consumer subsidy - BUDI95 quota restored to 300 litres, carried here on 1 September - and to have the listed utility absorb an electricity cost, with TENAGA taking RM120m to RM150m, covered on 21 September. Europe's proposed response, also carried on 21 September, is to tax energy producers. Thailand is proposing to give up tax revenue instead. Three states, three points on the same value chain; the comparison is drawn here.

The trigger has eased sharply in the latest session. This edition's own commodity table shows Nymex crude at USD95.8 a barrel, down 4.51%, against USD100.3 in the previous edition - so the measure is being floated into a market that has turned, not one still rising.

Thailand already runs the loosest policy rate in Kenanga's own table of thirteen, at 1.00%, recorded on this board on 21 September from its BoJ Economic Viewpoint. A fiscal fuel measure would be a second easing lever on top of that, not a first - which is a different position from Malaysia, whose OPR has sat at 2.75% for fourteen months.

It runs directly against the direction Kenanga expects in Malaysia. Its Budget Preview in this same bundle expects no major new taxes but a compliance, enforcement and collection-efficiency agenda that plugs leakages in an existing revenue base. A tax cut widens the gap that agenda is meant to close. No report in the 22 September bundle carries a Kenanga view on Thailand.

macro.h: Fed's Goolsbee says road to 2% inflation may not be painless
macro.body: Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago president Austan Goolsbee warned the central bank cannot ignore repeated and persistent supply shocks, and must respond in a way that may cause economic hardship. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: The content is a warning about method rather than a forecast. The central bank 'cannot ignore repeated and persistent supply shocks, and must respond in a way that may cause economic hardship'. No rate path, no vote, no meeting reference, no inflation figure and no time frame is attached, so nothing here is directly measurable.

It is the first Fed speaker on this board to concede the cost side out loud. The sequence has been about whether to hike - Warsh signalling hikes may be needed (1 September), the decision hanging on inflation (7 September), the hike case building (14 September), global banks expecting one (15 September) - and the 25bps hike delivered on 16 September. Goolsbee is the first to say what getting to 2% might cost.

It cuts against Kenanga's own position while agreeing with its diagnosis. This board recorded on 17 September that Kenanga called the September hike a policy error on the grounds that a funds rate does not fix a supply shock. Goolsbee accepts the shocks are supply-side and draws the opposite conclusion - that the Fed must respond anyway. The disagreement is about the response, not the cause; that framing is drawn here.

Kenanga's live base case is a hold, and this is the clearest challenge to it the board has carried since it was set. Its 21 September Bond Market Weekly Outlook states a base case that 'the latest Fed hike marks the end of the tightening cycle', with policy rates unchanged through end-2027. A sitting FOMC participant publicly preparing the ground for hardship-inducing policy is not what that base case assumes.

The market did not trade it as hawkish, and no causal link should be read into that. This edition's index table shows the Dow up 0.71% to 52,048.8, the S&P 500 up 1.49% to 7,764.7 and the NASDAQ up 2.26% to 27,122.1 on the 21 September session - the largest single-session gain in the NASDAQ this board has recorded in the period. It is context, not a response.

macro.h: ECB launches key link between blockchain and euro payment system
macro.body: The European Central Bank on Monday began letting banks settle tokenised wholesale transactions in central-bank money while continuing efforts to develop a digital euro for consumers by the end of the decade. (Reuters)
takeaways: There are two different things in one sentence and they run on different timelines. Wholesale settlement of tokenised transactions in central-bank money is live from Monday; the retail digital euro remains an effort to be developed 'by the end of the decade', four years out. The item does not separate them, and they are not the same project.

Nothing is sized. No participating bank count, no platform name, no transaction volume, no settlement value, no cost and no pilot period is given, so the launch cannot be measured against anything now or later.

It is plumbing, not policy. Settlement in central-bank money already exists; what changed is the ledger it can run on. No policy rate, no balance-sheet item and no inflation consequence follows from it, which is what distinguishes this from every other ECB item this board has carried.

It is the first European entry in weeks that is not about the energy shock or interest rates. The prior run was all shock response - the ECB hike on 11 September, Lagarde calling the inflation shock longer-lasting on 14 September, Kazaks seeing a growing case for tightening on 15 September, and the proposed EU windfall tax on energy companies on 21 September.

No Malaysian read-across is stated and none is available from the retrieved source. This board holds no Kenanga coverage of a Malaysian digital-asset or payments name, and the 22 September bundle carries no report on the euro area - its Economic Viewpoint is domestic and fiscal.

reports.flag: Four points of caution on this row, reported as printed rather than resolved. (1) The report carries three different share counts and two different market capitalisations. The Stock Information box gives 6,042.7m shares outstanding and a market cap of RM29,125.8m, but 6,042.7m at RM4.84 is RM29,246.6m - which is exactly the market cap the peer table on page 4 prints for GAMUDA. The sum-of-parts on page 2 uses a third figure, 5,929.0m issued shares, and that one reconciles internally (RM29,927.8m divided by 5,929.0m gives the RM5.05 SoP per share). Arithmetic here; the note reconciles none of them. (2) The core EPS history on page 3 cannot be reconciled with the growth figures on page 1. Page 3 prints core EPS of 32.3 sen for both FY2023A and FY2024A despite core net profit rising from RM859m to RM912m, then 16.9 sen for FY2025A on RM1,003m - a 47.7% fall in EPS against a 10.0% rise in profit. Page 1's Summary Earnings Table shows Core EPS Growth of +10.0% for FY2025A. Book value per share halves over the same period, from RM4.03 to RM2.02, which is consistent with a share count roughly doubling, but no corporate exercise is described anywhere in the note. Identified here; none of these figures is used as data on this row. (3) Three different return-on-equity series appear in the same document. Page 3's profitability block gives ROE of 3.4% for FY2025A rising to 4.8% in FY2027F, with ROA printed above ROE throughout (8.6% and 10.6%); the DuPont block immediately below gives a different ROE series (8.4% and 10.2%); and the page 4 peer table gives a 1-year forward ROE of 8.5%. Reproduced as printed. (4) The OUTPERFORM rating needs the dividend to clear Kenanga's own threshold. The rating definitions on page 5 define OUTPERFORM as expected total return of more than 10%, and the peer table's price upside is 9.5%; adding the 2.1% FY26F net dividend yield gives 11.6%, computed here. The note does not show that step. Two peer-table entries also sit well outside the rest of the table and are recorded as printed rather than used: KIMLUN at OUTPERFORM with 66.7% upside on a 4.1x forward core PER, and SUNCON at a 16.9x PBV on a 61.9% forward ROE.
reports.name: Gamuda Berhad
reports.catalyst: A fourth order-book milestone in four weeks, with nothing else moved. Transport for New South Wales awarded the 4.5km Elizabeth Drive Upgrade and 3km Mamre Road Upgrade Stage 2 project, worth about AUD2b in total and jointly funded by the Australian and New South Wales governments, to the 50:50 Gamuda Engineering Australia-BMD Constructions joint venture. The JV's contract portion is AUD624m (c.RM1.8b), giving GAMUDA a AUD312m (c.RM908m) revenue share. Work commences immediately with completion targeted by 2030, the contract carries rise-and-fall provisions similar to cost-plus terms, and PBT margin guidance is about 5%, consistent with GAMUDA's traditional Australian infrastructure work. The win lifts YTD FY27 contract wins to RM10.2b against a full-year assumption of RM27b and pushes the outstanding order book to a record RM62.5b - past the group's own RM50b end-2026 target - with Malaysia at 44% of the book and Australia at 35%. OUTPERFORM and the SoP-based TP of RM5.30 are both maintained, and all earnings and job-win assumptions are unchanged.
reports.quote: Just under three months into FY27, this win has lifted YTD contract wins to RM10.2b against our full-year assumption of RM27b.
summary: What moved and what did not, with every figure cross-checked. Nothing moved. The rating stays OUTPERFORM with the unchanged marker beside it, and the target price stays at RM5.30 - identical to the RM5.30 read from GAMUDA's own Company Updates on this board on 1 September and 7 September. The share price of RM4.84 matches this edition's own tables, where GAMUDA appears third by volume at 18.12m shares and sixth among top gainers at +1.3%. Forecasts are explicitly maintained: construction job-win assumptions of RM22b and RM27b for FY26 and FY27, and property sales targets of RM4b and RM5b. The valuation is unchanged in construction too - 22x CY27 PER, in line with IJM (OP; TP RM3.35) and SUNCON (OP; TP RM9.70) - giving a sum-of-parts of RM5.05 a share, plus a 5% premium of RM0.25 for a 4-star ESG rating, which sums exactly to RM5.30. The KLCI level printed in the report, 1,666.84, matches the 1,666.9 in this edition's own index table.

The contract, sized properly, and why the earnings effect is not the point. The JV portion is AUD624m of a c.AUD2b project; GAMUDA's 50% share is AUD312m, stated as c.RM908m, which implies an exchange rate of about RM2.91 to the Australian dollar - computed here, and consistent with the c.RM1.8b the note gives for the full AUD624m. At the guided PBT margin of about 5%, the whole RM908m revenue share is worth roughly RM45m of pre-tax profit spread over a build running to 2030, or something like RM11m a year - arithmetic here against an FY27F PBT of RM1,820m, which is about 0.6%. The rise-and-fall provisions matter more than the margin: they pass input-cost movements through, which is what makes a four-year Australian civil contract bookable at a stable 5% rather than exposed to the cost inflation this board has tracked all month.

The order book reconciles exactly against this board's own prior reading, which is the cleanest cross-check available. On 7 September this board read, from GAMUDA's own Company Update PDF, an outstanding order book of RM61.6b and YTD FY27 job wins of RM9.3b following the Parramatta Integrated Station Development award. Add today's RM908m to each and you get RM62.5b and RM10.2b - the two figures this note prints. Both bridges computed here, and neither document draws them. On the stated geographic split, Malaysia's 44% of RM62.5b is about RM27.5b and Australia's 35% about RM21.9b; the remaining 21%, roughly RM13.1b, is unallocated in the note. YTD wins of RM10.2b are 37.8% of the RM27b full-year assumption less than three months into a July financial year.

The pipeline is substantial and entirely unsecured, and the forecasts already assume most of it lands. Kenanga names the Springhill data centre campus, where GAMUDA has swept all four contracts awarded since April and is called the frontrunner for upcoming tenders; the Northern Perak water project domestically; a 'high probability' of another Taiwan project by 2HCY26; and shortlistings for Brisbane infrastructure and the Northland Corridor Highway in New Zealand. The FY27 step-up they support is steep: revenue +31.4% to RM23.0b, core net profit +31.3% to RM1,388m, core EPS 23.4 sen, and the PER compressing from 27.2x to 20.7x on an unchanged RM4.84. Kenanga sits 1.7% above the consensus it prints for FY26F (RM1,057m against RM1,039.6m) and 2.5% above for FY27F (RM1,388m against RM1,354.3m) - computed here, so the disagreement with the street is small. Cash flow is the strain: free cash flow of -RM1,575m in FY26F turning to +RM1,906m in FY27F, with net gearing peaking at 0.70x in FY26F before returning to 0.56x, and the dividend held flat at 10.0 sen throughout.

Why this row reads None stated, and a peer table that agrees with this board on every line. The investment case opens 'We continue to like GAMUDA for: (i) its strong positioning in upcoming data centre tenders, (ii) its ability to secure overseas projects, (iii) its robust earnings visibility underpinned by a record outstanding order book of RM62.5b, and (iv) its inroads into the renewable energy space.' Searching all five pages for this board's full conviction list returns only that construction and nothing for top pick, sector pick, our pick, preferred, most attractive, favour or favourite. This board treats 'we continue to like' as investment-case language rather than a pick declaration - the same treatment given TENAGA on 21 September, KEYFIELD on 18 September, MISC on 17 September and BAUTO on 11 September - so the Kenanga Signal reads None stated. Separately, all four covered peers in the page 4 table reconcile exactly with targets this board has read from those companies' own PDFs: IJM at OUTPERFORM with RM3.35 (27 August), KIMLUN at OUTPERFORM with RM1.50 (27 August), SUNCON at OUTPERFORM with RM9.70 (24 and 26 August) and KERJAYA at OUTPERFORM with RM3.80 (4 September). Not one target in the table disagrees with this board's record, which is unusual enough to be worth stating.

analyst.note: No named non-Kenanga house declares a pick on GAMUDA in a dated, publicly retrievable note read during this run, so this row's Analyst Signal reads None stated. No named house had published a retrievable note on the Elizabeth Drive / Mamre Road award as at the time of this run. The award itself is independently confirmed: The Star's 'Trading ideas' column of 22 September 2026 carries the A$624.0m (RM1.8b) contract from Transport for New South Wales for the Elizabeth Drive Upgrade - Mamre Road Upgrade Stage 2 in Western Sydney, matching Kenanga's own figures, and Construction Briefing reports the same award with the scope split 50/50 between Gamuda and BMD Constructions on a design-and-construct basis. TA used no pick language in the retrieved report, so this row reads None stated. The divergence flag is not set: TA's buy at RM5.42 sits on the same side as Kenanga's OUTPERFORM at RM5.30. Two earlier dated calls also stand, both reported by the New Straits Times on 14 August 2026: Public Investment Bank maintained 'Outperform' at RM5.60 and Hong Leong Investment Bank reiterated 'Buy' at RM5.27; neither used pick language either. reports.flag: Five points of caution on this row, reported as printed rather than resolved. (1) This report is filed under a 21 September date but is carried here as a 22 September publication, and the reason matters. The filename is EV_MY-2027-Federal-Budget-Preview_260921.pdf - without the usual -Kenanga suffix - and the PDF's own page header reads 21 September 2026; Kenanga's website lists it on the 21 September bundle page. But it appears nowhere in the 21 September Kenanga Today digest: a search of that document for the word 'budget' returns no hits. It is announced for the first time in the 22 September digest's Macro Bits, with the standard '(See Economic Viewpoint: Malaysia 2027 Federal Budget Preview)' pointer, while that edition's Ideas of the Day line names only GAMUDA. Under rules/signals.md §1 the day's line-up is taken from the digest's own bundle contents rather than the Ideas of the Day line, precisely because that line omits macro publications - which is this case exactly. The row therefore sits on 22 September. Precedent for an irregular filename date is MBMR, filed as 260808 for a 28 August report. Identified here, and no existing date's file was altered. (2) The nominal-GDP derivation in the second takeaway is inferred, not read. It is computed from the note's own overall balance of -RM83.0b against deficit ratios printed to one decimal place, which leaves a wide rounding band - the implied 2027 nominal GDP growth of about 8.6% could be anywhere from roughly 5.6% to 11.6%. The direction of the argument survives that band; the magnitude does not. Nothing in the note states any nominal GDP figure. (3) The note declares its own central commodity assumption stale. Table 2 runs on average Brent of USD80/bbl for 2026 and USD74/bbl for 2027, and a footnote states the assumption is under review with the revision to be 'higher (around USD90/bbl average for 2026, USD80/bbl for 2027)', with the fiscal arithmetic to be updated once the new oil view is finalised. This edition's own commodity table shows Nymex crude at USD95.8/bbl on the 21 September session - above even the unpublished revision, computed here. Since the note attributes the 2027 revenue decline specifically to a lower Brent assumption, every revenue and deficit figure on this row is provisional on Kenanga's own statement. (4) Typographical and editorial slips carried as printed: the overview reads 'We project the 2026 deficit to edge up 3.8% of GDP' with a word missing; the political-economy section carries a duplicated, broken sentence - 'The latest reporting points to 2Q27 as the working assumption. Even that as the working assumption inside the coalition.'; the supply-side paragraph ends 'despite lingering global trade policy uncertainty over.'; and the fiscal outlook reads 'as the government prioritise domestic demand'. (5) This is an Economic Viewpoint and carries no stock call, so the rating, target-price and share-price columns are empty by design and no Analyst Signal is sought.
reports.name: Malaysia 2027 Federal Budget Preview: Merdeka giveaways set election pace; revenue base stays narrow
reports.catalyst: Kenanga's preview of Budget 2027, to be tabled on 9 October 2026 - the fifth MADANI Budget and the second year of the 13th Malaysia Plan, built around ten focus areas aimed mainly at cost of living and the M40 group, with growth priorities in AI, semiconductors and the digital economy. The central claim is that there is no revenue-reform pillar this year: Focus Area Five, the closest thing to one, covers tax compliance, subsidy management and spending efficiency, and 'plugs leakages in an existing base rather than widening it'. Kenanga reads this as a pre-election budget on a shorter runway than the February 2028 deadline implies, with 2Q27 as its working assumption for GE16, and points to the Merdeka Eve package of 30 August - six measures effective 1 September, including a BUDI95 quota restoration the Prime Minister admitted was meant for Budget 2027 - as the tell. It forecasts the federal deficit at 3.8% of GDP in 2026 narrowing to 3.5% in 2027, revenue falling to RM365.0b from RM370.0b, net expenditure narrowing to RM448.0b from RM453.0b, 2027 GDP growth of 5.0% against an expected government target of 4.5%-5.5%, and debt-to-GDP easing to 62.2%. Its market conclusion is to fade ringgit or long-end rallies that price a GST-style revenue story into the budget.
reports.quote: We would fade ringgit or long-end rallies that price a GST-style revenue story into Budget 2027.
summary: The headline call, and the fact that the improving ratio is not an improving budget. Kenanga forecasts the deficit at 3.8% of GDP in 2026 (2025: 3.7%; the Ministry of Finance's own 2026 estimate: 3.5%) narrowing to 3.5% in 2027. But its own Table 2 shows the overall balance unchanged at -RM83.0b in both years, and revenue falling to RM365.0b from RM370.0b. The entire ratio improvement therefore comes from the denominator, which the note states outright: 'the improvement in the ratio comes from nominal GDP growth rather than from stronger collection.' On the spending side, net expenditure narrows to RM448.0b from RM453.0b, operating expenditure falls to RM364.0b from RM369.5b, and development expenditure rises to RM85.0b from RM84.0b. Every line of the table reconciles: RM364.0b plus RM85.0b is RM449.0b gross, less RM1.0b of loan recoveries is RM448.0b net, and RM365.0b less RM448.0b is exactly -RM83.0b. All three checks computed here.

What the unchanged deficit implies about nominal growth, and why it needs a caveat. Taking -RM83.0b at 3.8% of GDP puts 2026 nominal GDP at about RM2,184b, and the same RM83.0b at 3.5% puts 2027 at about RM2,371b - implying nominal growth of about 8.6%, against about 7.3% implied for 2026 on the same method and about RM2,035b for 2025. So nominal growth would have to accelerate while Kenanga's own real growth forecast slows to 5.0% from 5.3%, which requires the GDP deflator to rise to roughly 3.6% from about 2.0%. That is difficult to square with a 2026 inflation forecast of 1.9%, recorded on this board from Kenanga's own CPI note on 21 September, and with a lower Brent assumption for 2027. Every figure in this takeaway is computed here and none appears in the note; because the deficit ratios are printed to one decimal place the implied growth carries a wide rounding band - see the flag on this row.

The thesis, in Kenanga's own words: there is no revenue chapter. 'Notably, there is no revenue-reform pillar this year.' Focus Area Five - 'spending that delivers the best value for the people' - covers tax compliance, subsidy management and spending efficiency, and 'plugs leakages in an existing base rather than widening it', which Kenanga contrasts explicitly with Budget 2026's Medium-Term Revenue Strategy framing that flagged base-broadening. The Prime Minister has ruled out a broad-based tax while being open to studying 'acceptable GST features' within SST; Kenanga reads that as invoice-level matching through MyInvois, less cascading via better input relief and rationalised exemption scope - 'not a GST comeback'. Its contrarian flag is stated as such: 'don't mistake GST features for GST's return. Markets pricing a base-broadening story risk disappointment.' On revenue, it expects no major new taxes, with collections supported instead by the expanded SST framework, wider e-invoicing adoption, the Global Minimum Tax and administration reform - while noting that e-invoicing coverage 'has been pushed back rather than completed', which it calls the clearest evidence the plumbing is unfinished.

The political-economy call, which is the most forward-leaning thing in the note. Kenanga reads Budget 2027 as a pre-election budget on a working assumption of GE16 in 2Q27, well inside the February 2028 deadline, and its evidence is the Merdeka Eve address of 30 August: six cost-of-living and business-relief measures effective 1 September, in which the Prime Minister admitted the BUDI95 and Budi Diesel quota restoration was originally meant for Budget 2027 and was moved forward. Kenanga's reading of that is unusually direct - 'The fiscal cost is trivial, which is precisely what makes it a signal rather than a spending decision. A government willing to break its own Budget sequencing for a measure this cheap is optimising for the calendar, not the ledger.' It sizes the incremental BUDI95 cost at RM0.5b to RM1.0b over September to December, some 2 to 5 basis points of GDP, and notes that average usage runs at about 100 litres a month with fewer than 1.0% of users consistently exceeding 200 litres, so the old cap rarely bound. The risk it flags is repetition rather than this package: if the election comes earlier or BUDI95-style reversals and SARA top-ups keep arriving outside the budget cycle, it puts the 2027 deficit closer to 3.6%-3.7%. This board has carried the six measures themselves - the quota restoration to 300 litres was recorded on 1 September.

The tradeable conclusions, checked against spot and against this board's own record. Kenanga maintains its end-2026 USD/MYR forecast at 3.95 and revises its end-2026 10-year MGS yield forecast up to 3.88% from 3.63%, while keeping USD/MYR at 3.90 for end-2027 on the Fed cutting from 2Q27 - framing the caution as 'tactical into the October tabling, not a change to our constructive MYR call'. Against this edition's own forex table, USD/MYR closed at 4.0778 on 21 September, so the end-2026 call requires about 3.1% of ringgit appreciation in roughly three months, computed here. And this board read the 10-year MGS at 3.917% on 18 September from Kenanga's own Bond Market Weekly Outlook, so even the raised 3.88% end-2026 forecast still sits below where the market was four days earlier. Three verifiable signals would change the view: e-invoicing coverage gaps closing, a published tax expenditure statement, or arrears-collection data showing real progress - Malaysia currently publishes neither a tax expenditure statement nor its stock of uncollected arrears, which the note calls the first problem to fix. On the balance sheet, federal debt eases to 62.2% of GDP in 2027 from 63.7% in 2026 and 65.2% in 2025, with debt service charges at 16.5% of revenue against 16.8% - still above the government's self-imposed 15.0% threshold - on gross issuance of RM184.8b. Sovereign ratings of A3/Stable, A-/Stable and BBB+/Stable are expected to hold, with an upgrade seen as unlikely before 2029.
